description:
We are a passionate team of Computer Systems Engineering students from Mexico, driven by innovation, technology, and the desire to create solutions with real-world impact.

Our interests include software development, artificial intelligence, data science, Earth observation, and emerging technologies. We are especially excited about combining scientific research with creative engineering to develop meaningful, accessible, and innovative experiences.
summary:
The hearthbeats of the earth is an interactive, inclusive web platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It answers the challenge of creating an “Earth Jukebox.”

It transforms visualizations from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) into soundscapes generated in real time, so that Earth and space science can be heard, not just seen.

It is designed especially for blind and visually impaired people. It combines a 3D representation of the Earth with voice-narrated descriptions and dynamic sounds that change according to the data in each image.

Our purpose is to show that space and our planet can be not only observed, but also heard and experienced.
details:
“Earth’s Heartbeats” is our “Earth Jukebox”: it turns NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into sound. We have four 3D views of the Earth: aurora borealis, ocean waves, clouds, and continental temperature. In each one, we analyze the colors (RGB/HSV) and their intensity, and translate them into frequencies and volume in real time.

It makes Earth science accessible to people with visual disabilities, with nothing to install: you just open the web page. It is also an educational tool that makes science more engaging and multisensory for everyone.

NASA’s EIC produces stunning visualizations, but presenting science only through images limits its reach. We expand that reach: we bring knowledge of our planet to more people, promote inclusion in science communication, and show that NASA’s data can also be heard and experienced.

We used JavaScript, the Web Audio API (with OscillatorNode for frequencies and GainNode for volume), and Three.js for the 3D Earth. As our base resource, we used NASA’s EIC images. All you need is a computer or device with a browser and audio.

Each view has its own voice: the aurora sounds according to its color and intensity; the waves, according to their movement; the clouds, according to their density; and continental temperature, with lower or higher tones depending on the heat. The sounds are not downloaded files: they are generated with code in real time, so every experience is dynamic.

Three main factors guided our design and development: accessibility, with visually impaired users in mind; fidelity to the EIC data, so the sound reflects what the images show; and musical experience, so it is pleasant to listen to. We also made sure it was lightweight and worked in any browser.
